text.p: The lira closed easier at 104,050 against the dollar on Tuesday versus Monday's 103,980 despite the central bank's dollar sales in the afternoon.

Bankers said the lira weakened to 104,430 at midday on banks' dollar demand and lack of sellers, prompting central bank intervention. It began selling dollars for lira in early afternoon to restrain the U.S. currency's rise after which the lira firmed.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 104,150 lira at the opening, after Monday's 103,850 lira close, but later lowered it to 104,050 in line with the dollar's drop against mark in world markets.
The money market opened with a 20.3 trillion lira surplus. Overnight money dived to 58 percent at close from an opening of 77.75 percent, and compared to Monday's 77.76 percent average.
The central bank funded banks 5.2 trillion lira via tomorrow next value deals at 76 percent, down sharply from the 18.3 trillion lira it injected via t/n on Monday.
The central bank did not lend overnight money, against Monday's 4.9 trillion lira overnight funding at 78 percent.

Yields on t-bills and bonds climbed by as much as two points in correction to a week-long downward move. Yields had plunged by a total of six to seven points due to a buying spree prompted by easier money rates since last Tuesday.

The average yield on the most heavily traded Sept 3, 1997 paper rose to 112.67 from Monday's 111.30 percent. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 113.24, up from Friday's 111.64 percent average.
